reviews.review: I love this game. I wish there was more similar to it. I have recommended it to my friends.

Only 2 thing about this game bothers me
- Game is too short. Game could easily have been 2-3 times as long - more missions that aren't directly linked to the main plot would make sense and be great. 
- The super-blurred cutscenes. Not a big problem for me when I encountered them  - but at some point you need to use the information from them to solve a game-puzzle that story-wise should be 100% obvious to the Tanner character you play, but is obscured to the player. That felt like a very bad design decision.

This game had me engrossed from the start. If you like action, this isn't for you. But if you're a cozy gamer, it's great. Very immersive - I felt like a real Operator. I still have more achievements to unlock so maybe I'll get a different ending with different choices!

--- BUY THIS GAME WHEN IT IS ON SALE ---

I paid ~ $13.00 and that is TOO much for this game. I think a fair price for this game is $5.00 due to play hours and lack of replayability.

PROs:

+ I like investigative puzzle games and this one was intriguing.
+ Story was compelling.
+ I liked the idea of using different systems to discover information and link said information together.
+ I am looking forward to a sequel. Hopefully it will be longer than this game.

CONs:

- I beat it twice in 7 hours so average game play time was 3.5 hours. I really only played it twice to get the achievements though.
     - I don't think the price of the game should be this high for such a short game. Especially since there isn't a lot of replayability with this game :/.
- The story gives the illusion of choice but regardless of dialogue options, you still end up where you are intended to go; very RAILROADY
- The game has investigative tools but for most of them you only use them once throughout the entire game.
- For my second playthrough, I was REALLY wanting a skip button for scenes where the protagonist "goes home at the end of the day;" It was really boring to sit through those scenes.
- There are some locked files that you don't get access to, which was disappointing. There were many missed opportunities to build lore or give players opportunities to poke around, even if they resulted in dead ends, it would have been nice to fill out the world a little more.
- It would have been nice if there was a reward/punishment system for being smart or needing to have your hand held through the whole game. Some sort of variable input that would impact the game based on player actions. Like a trust meter so if people trust you, it is easier to lie to them or something.

I know it sounds like I am taking a huge dump on this game but my goal is to help the developers with the sequel.The game has A LOT of good ideas, I just think the execution and the offering could have been better.

That being said, I liked the game and I want to see more from this developer.

[h3][b]spoiler alert[/b][/h3]

What makes this game even more disturbing is that it purposely references events that actually happened. Back in the 50s and 60s, CIA was responsible for several illegal experiments on people without their consent for "military purposes" under [b]Project MKUltra[/b], just like in the game... dosing them with drugs, conducting harsh interviews, and trying to implant false memories or break down minds for their own purpose, and even using all the UFO sightings events to misdirect attention and hide all that bs. [i]The Operator[/i] captures that exact atmosphere: the manipulation, the paranoia, the feeling that even your own thoughts might not be yours.

This game was very enjoyable if you are into the Delta Green/ X Files conspiracy thriller genre. You are looking at about 4 hours of game play for your first play through, but I am excited to go back and do a second one. The whole game is a virtual desktop, matching clues and digging through databases. I wish the puzzles were harder and more involved, as the game introduces several mechanics it uses once and then never gets seen again. It would have been better to see more "normal" cases before it goes off the deep end. The story was more central and better written than I expected, with actual emotional moments and great twists. 

Overall I recommend it to any gamer who like puzzles and conspiracy thrillers, but I just wish I had more of it.
